---
title: "PX4 SITL Setup"
---

This page covers how to build PX4 firmware, launch the Gazebo SITL simulator,
and wire it into the pixi workspace for use with the ROS 2 integration.

---

## Prerequisites

PX4 SITL requires a native Ubuntu build environment. The PX4 source tree is
**not** managed inside the ROS 2 workspace — it lives separately and is built
with its own toolchain.

```bash
# Install PX4 build dependencies (run once)
git clone https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot.git --recursive
cd PX4-Autopilot
bash ./Tools/setup/ubuntu.sh
```

::: {.callout-note}
`ubuntu.sh` installs system packages including `gcc-arm-none-eabi`, `ninja`,
and Python dependencies. It also installs `gz-harmonic` (Gazebo) for SITL.
Re-run it if a new PX4 checkout changes the required dependencies.
:::

---

## Building PX4 for Gazebo SITL

```bash
cd PX4-Autopilot
make px4_sitl gz_x500
```

This compiles the SITL binary and generates a Gazebo world with the x500
quadrotor model. The first build takes ~5 minutes; subsequent builds are
incremental.

To confirm the build succeeded:

```bash
ls build/px4_sitl_default/bin/px4
```

---

## Launching SITL standalone

```bash
cd PX4-Autopilot
make px4_sitl gz_x500
```

On launch, PX4 prints its version string (`PX4 v1.16.x`) and the Gazebo window
opens with the x500 model on the ground.

To choose a different vehicle model:

```bash
make px4_sitl gz_x500_depth        # x500 with depth camera
make px4_sitl gz_x500_lidar        # x500 with lidar
make px4_sitl gz_rc_cessna         # fixed-wing
```

---

## Key environment variables

PX4 SITL reads several environment variables at launch. Set them before calling
`make` or running the PX4 binary directly.

| Variable | Purpose | Example |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `PX4_GZ_MODEL` | Override the vehicle model name | `x500` |
| `PX4_GZ_WORLD` | Override the Gazebo world file | `default` |
| `PX4_SYS_AUTOSTART` | Airframe ID (overrides the model default) | `4001` |
| `PX4_GZ_MODEL_POSE` | Initial spawn pose `x,y,z,roll,pitch,yaw` | `0,0,0.1,0,0,0` |
| `HEADLESS` | Disable the Gazebo GUI (useful on servers) | `1` |

Example — spawn in a custom pose without the GUI:

```bash
HEADLESS=1 PX4_GZ_MODEL_POSE="0,0,0.5,0,0,1.57" make px4_sitl gz_x500
```

---

## Integrating with the pixi workspace

The recommended pattern is to store the path to the PX4 source tree as a pixi
variable and expose it as an environment variable in the activation script.

**`pixi.toml`**:

```toml
[workspace.variables]
PX4_SRC = "/home/user/PX4-Autopilot"

[activation]
scripts = ["activate.sh"]
env = { PX4_AUTOPILOT = "$PX4_SRC" }
```

Then the launch task can start PX4 directly:

```toml
[tasks]
px4 = { cmd = "cd $PX4_AUTOPILOT && make px4_sitl gz_x500" }
```

Or launch from a Python launch file using `subprocess` inside a ROS 2 launch
action (see the launch file pattern in the Package Setup page).

---

## Confirming SITL is running

Once PX4 starts, the NuttShell prompt appears:

```
nsh>
```

Check that the EKF has initialised and that the vehicle is ready:

```
nsh> ekf2 status
nsh> commander status
```

In a second terminal, confirm the DDS bridge topics are visible after starting
the micro-XRCE-DDS agent (see [DDS Agent Setup](uxrce-dds-agent.qmd)):

```bash
ros2 topic list | grep fmu
```

---

## Troubleshooting

### Gazebo window does not open

The display is not forwarded. Either set `HEADLESS=1`, or on a remote machine
export `DISPLAY=:0` before running SITL.

### `make px4_sitl gz_x500` fails with missing submodules

The PX4 repo was cloned without `--recursive`:

```bash
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

### PX4 exits immediately after launch

Lockstep mode is waiting for a Gazebo clock. Ensure Gazebo is running — the
`gz_x500` target launches both. If you are running the PX4 binary directly
(without `make`), launch Gazebo first.

### `EKF2 ERROR` at startup

Normal on the first few seconds while sensors initialise. If it persists past
~10 s the IMU or barometer simulation is misconfigured — check that `gz-harmonic`
is installed and that the Gazebo sensors plugin loaded without errors in the
terminal output.
